samples.summary: No test for the case-insensitive `data:` detection the diff explicitly fixes
samples.evidence: `imageInline` was changed from `image.src.startsWith('data:')` to `/^data:/i.test(image.src)`, and the comment states the old spelling let an uppercase `DATA:image/...` src be emitted inline even with `inlineImages` off. Every data-URI test in markdown.test.ts (lines 343, 361, 385, 669) and in the new CLI suite uses lowercase `data:`, so reverting the regex to `startsWith('data:')` would leave the whole suite green (SAFE_IMAGE_DATA_URI is already `/i`, so the uppercase URL would sail through). Grepped `DATA:image|Data:image` across packages — no matches.

samples.summary: The proxy's `set` trap (refusing reassignment of `setPageSetup`) has no test
samples.evidence: `pageSetupGuardedStore`'s `set` trap returns `false` for `setPageSetup` specifically so the guard cannot be overwritten. editor-page-setup.test.ts and editor-read-only.test.ts only ever *call* `getStore().setPageSetup(...)` (grep of `setPageSetup` across packages/docs/test shows no assignment). Deleting the `set` trap — restoring the unvalidated write for anything that assigns over the method — would not fail any test.

samples.summary: `sectPrLengthPx`'s `allowZero` distinction is only half covered: a legitimate zero margin is never asserted
samples.evidence: The helper's stated contract is that a page dimension of 0 is rejected while a margin of 0 is a legitimate edge-to-edge layout. The new suite tests zero page size (line 187) and non-numeric/negative margins (lines 195-201), but no case feeds `<w:pgMar w:top="0" .../>` and asserts the 0 survives. Flipping `allowZero` to `false` for margins (silently replacing an author's 0" margin with 96 px on every import) would keep the suite green.

samples.summary: `fitMargins`' proportional-shrink behavior is untested — only "content box > 0" is asserted
samples.evidence: `fitMargins` is documented as shrinking a margin pair *proportionally* "so a document whose margins are merely too large for its page keeps the ratio its author chose". The new test 'leaves a positive content box when margins would close it' uses an equal 5000/5000 pair and asserts only that the remaining box is positive, which would also pass if the implementation reset both margins to the defaults or zeroed them. No test uses an asymmetric pair (e.g. 4000/1000) and checks the ratio is preserved.

samples.summary: The ruler margin-drag path now goes through the throwing `writePageSetup` with no test over that wiring
samples.evidence: `ruler.onMarginChange` was rewritten to call `writePageSetup`, which calls `assertUsablePageSetup` and can throw a RangeError mid-drag. Grepping `onMarginChange` in packages/docs finds only the ruler source and this call site — no test drives the ruler callback into the editor, so neither the happy path (drag still repaginates in one undo step) nor the refusal path (a drag that would close the box) is covered. The new editor-page-setup.test.ts exercises only the `EditorAPI`/`getStore()` doors.

samples.summary: `LINE_SEPARATORS` covers NEL/U+2028/U+2029 but only CR/LF are tested
samples.evidence: The new escaping tests ('keeps a blank line in an image alt…', 'keeps a blank line in a text run…', table-cell case) all use `\n`. No test feeds U+0085, U+2028 or U+2029, so removing them from the character class would go unnoticed.

samples.summary: Slides md export pins only the link gate, not the image gate
samples.evidence: The docs CLI suite covers both hrefs and image srcs (including the `inlineImages` default), while the new slides suite adds a `link()` helper only and asserts hrefs. An image src regression on the slides md path (the second consumer of the same serializer, which the comment itself argues needs pinning at the command boundary) would not be caught here.
